_about: Multi-cell DCM Warp hybrid (per-cell turgor + cortex edges + node-node cohesion + node-face contact, all device-resident) + host remesh. gbook RTX A5000, measured 2026-06-21. icosphere subdiv=2 (162 nodes/cell).
integration: all 4 committed parity-verified inter/intra-cell Warp kernels wired into one device-resident per-step loop on a shared node-pool; host remesh_pass + resync (multi-cell validated: 648->672 nodes via splits; remesh sync <1% of runtime).
finding: Intra-cell forces (turgor+edges) are FAST and fully GPU-resident (10.7k steps/s = same as single-cell). The bottleneck is the BRUTE-FORCE inter-cell pair search in the committed kernels: node-face contact is O(N*M) with the per-pair Ericson closest-point-on-triangle (dominant, -> 86 steps/s), cohesion is O(N^2) (secondary, -> 405). These kernels were written for PARITY (correctness), not speed; their own docstrings note production would use a neighbour list.
next_lever: Warp hash-grid (wp.HashGrid) neighbour list -> contact/cohesion become O(N*k) (k~tens of local neighbours) instead of O(N*M)/O(N^2). For 4 cells M=1280, k~30 => ~40x fewer pairs; expected to lift the all-forces multi-cell throughput toward the intra-cell 10k ceiling. The node-face grid (faces by AABB/centroid + node query) is the larger of the two.
remesh_note: remesh sync_frac < 1% at n_cells=8 period 500 -> remesh is NOT the multi-cell bottleneck (unlike single-cell where it was the only host cost); the inter-cell brute force dominates.
